title: 4 World Trade Center
status: Original reconstruction references; maximum fidelity and geographic review pending

facts: Completed 2013; 977 feet, about 298 m; marketed as 72 floors, with 56 office floors.
Lower office plan is a parallelogram; upper office plan is a trapezoid.
Facade uses colorless silver reflective glass. Approximately 11,000 unitized panes, nominally 5 feet wide by 13 feet 6 inches tall, with horizontal touch mullions concealing spandrels.
visualObservations: First photograph: distant silver tower silhouette and offset upper section, behind memorial buildings.
Second photograph: memorial pool foreground, very tall slender lobby mullions and low entrance doors behind.

Third photograph: lobby has pale ceiling/floor, dark polished core walls, light wood portals, tall vertical glazing and revolving doors. Suspended curved wire sculpture is visible; no exact geometry inferred.

Main vertical exterior photograph shows very fine flush panel joints and a separate upper plane behind the terrace edge. Final image is a distant Manhattan skyline view; it does not establish roof equipment or entrance geometry.

references.role: Architect Fumihiko Maki's 2019 lecture and published diagrams
visualObservations: Upper plan removes a large triangular area from the northwest portion of the lower plan; it is a constant vertical trapezoid above the terrace, not a continuously tapering solid.
Lower plan has separate stepped notches at northeast and southwest obtuse corners.
Section distinguishes lower lobby/retail, mechanical floors, long office stack, terrace/mechanical transfer and upper office stack/crown. No dimension labels are readable in this raster.
references.limits: Nominal page north and floor labels require signed map registration. Do not distribute images or trace them as an exact survey.

facts: Lobby finished ceiling is 46 feet.
Typical slab-to-slab height is stated as 13 feet 5 inches.
references.planDiscovery: Availability viewer > Floor 28 > View Floorplan opens a public PDF.
references.planInspection: Rendered and inspected. Proposed office fit-out, with north up, Greenwich Street left/west, Church Street right/east, Liberty Street bottom/south. Confirms the six-corner silhouette. No exterior dimensions or survey scale shown. Do not equate rentable square feet with geometric floor area.

facts: Opened November 2013.
Outdoor terrace at floor 57.
Five retail levels: ground, two below and two above.
Recessed obtuse southwest and northeast glass corners.
Architectural and tip height 297.7 m; occupied height 279.9 m.
65 above-ground floors, four below, versus marketed 72 labels.
Database lists completion 2014, while architect/owner report opening in 2013.
references.limits: Do not turn 72 marketed labels into 72 identical floor intervals. Preserve completion/opening conventions.

references.role: Richard B. Garlock of LERA, April 2015 Modern Steel Construction
facts: Lower office floors labelled 15-54; upper floors 57-72.
Perimeter has long clear spans and column-free corners; mechanical levels contain full-floor-depth trusses.
references.limits: Indexed PDF text inspected. Direct download returned HTTP 522; no local PDF available. A different lera.com search result returned an unrelated 127-page forensic practice brochure and was excluded. The publisher’s www.aisc.org version was found in search but returned HTTP 403 when opened; no local copy.

references.role: Benson facade supplier, now Permasteelisa Group
facts: Custom unitized curtain wall, steel and aluminium shopfronts, revolving and balanced doors, and extruded aluminium vertical storm-proof louvres.
visualObservations: Ground-level facade close-ups show flush large glass units with very fine dark joints, a deep recessed vertical corner and narrower return glazing.
Visible mechanical bands use alternating narrow vertical dark louvre strips and silver/glazed strips rather than a solid dark horizontal block.
Aerial header looks over the tower toward Brookfield Place and the Hudson River, showing the corner recess and plant strips. The upper roof is cropped; this is not a roof-equipment survey.

references.role: LERA, original structural engineer, project description
facts: Forty lower office floors labelled 15–54 and sixteen upper floors labelled 57–72.
Core-to-perimeter lease spans are 45 ft west/north/south and 35 ft east.
Four perimeter columns per side; 80 ft clear main spans, with corner cantilevers ranging 20–45 ft.
references.limits: An 80 ft clear span is not an 80 ft column-center distance. Do not scale a scanned drawing as though those measurements were equivalent.

references.role: Elevator supplier, Next Floor September 2014, pages 6–9
facts: Ground lobby has a 46 ft finished ceiling, glass on three sides, polished black granite core walls, marble and anigre accents.
Forty lower and sixteen upper office floors.
references.limits: Indexed text inspected. Web PDF screenshots failed with a cache error, so its photographs have not been visually reviewed. The architect’s separate lobby photograph was inspected.

references.role: New York City Office of Technology and Innovation, public Building Footprints
facts: One photogrammetric outline, last edited 2021-06-15. Attributes ground elevation 15 and roof height 978.45258 require units/datum review before use.
Minimum rectangle of returned WGS84 polygon: 84.806 by 60.413 m, heading -0.514574228923, center [-74.01202446363833,40.710325630096264]. Broadly confirms OSM ground envelope.
references.limits: City metadata resolves the apparent area mismatch: shape_area 7966.484375 is Web Mercator derived, not physical square metres. The projected WGS84 polygon is about 4577.46 square metres. Neither measures a typical office floor; the overhead perimeter does not identify setback levels.

references.role: City of New York municipal 3D model distribution
facts: Based on 2014 aerial survey; community-district Rhino 3dm files include six building line/surface sublayers and ground elevations.
About 100 iconic buildings have detailed roof structure; others use generalized LOD 1.5 geometry.
references.limits: Downloaded the current Manhattan Community District 1 archive through the replacement City page and inspected its six building layers in feet and State Plane coordinates. No usable tower geometry was present at this exact location. No municipal geometry is redistributed; see municipalArchive below.

facts: shape_area and shape_length are Web Mercator derived attributes and must not be used for physical measurements.
Roof height is relative to ground elevation, while ground elevation is a lowest-point datum, generally NAVD88 for modern collection.

mapEvidence.limits: Outline includes lower projections and is not a pure parallelogram. Do not stretch either office plan to its entire bounding rectangle.

remaining: Reconcile owner slab interval 13 ft 5 in with architect unit height 13 ft 6 in.
Derive external lower/upper plan measurements and corner recess depths from a dimensioned plan or mapped building parts.
Reconcile 65 physical floors with 72 marketed labels and mechanical levels.
Inspect close exterior images of roof plant, terrace, podium, revolving doors and vertical louvres.
Verify signed facade fit, pavement contact and maximum fidelity. The original source recipe, shared graphs, import and rendered captures are now implemented.
imagePolicy: Browser-only reference photos; one technical owner plan retained in ignored research artifacts. No reference image is redistributed.

planRegistration.status: Unresolved; do not extrude the entire ground envelope as a typical office floor
observations: Owner level-28 plan and architect lower plan share opposing northeast/southwest recessed corners.
Architect upper plan removes a northwest triangular region from the lower floor outline; surviving facade edges retain the recessed corners.
Retained OSM ground outline is wider and has a different set of projections. The plan geometry must be independently fitted to the site.
Map native +X at heading -0.513459789133 points east-southeast; +Z points south-southwest. Drawing north annotation has not yet been registered to that frame.

municipalArchive.inspection: 132223 objects, native feet. Examined all six building curve/surface layers within 180 ft of the exact BIN footprint center, including large overlapping objects. No tower roof/facade at this site was present. Do not infer setback elevations from this dataset.
